works.title: Letter to Mr. Storie, 1636
works.source: Oliver Cromwell · The Letters and Speeches of Oliver Cromwell, ed. Carlyle (Lomas edition) · public domain
works.note: Cromwell’s earliest surviving letter — urging a London friend to keep funding a Puritan lecture, and closing with the phrase that became his signature: “I beseech you… in the bowels of Christ Jesus.”

works.title: Letter to Mrs. St. John, 1638
works.source: Oliver Cromwell · The Letters and Speeches of Oliver Cromwell, ed. Carlyle (Lomas edition) · public domain
works.note: A letter of spiritual self-examination to his cousin — “I live in Mesheck… in Kedar” — one of the most personal glimpses of his inner religious life before the war.

works.title: After Marston Moor: Letter to Colonel Walton, 1644
works.source: Oliver Cromwell · The Letters and Speeches of Oliver Cromwell, ed. Carlyle (Lomas edition) · public domain
works.note: His dispatch after the great victory — “God made them as stubble to our swords” — turning mid-letter to console his brother-in-law on the battlefield death of his son. One of the most moving letters in the English language.

works.title: After Naseby: Letter to the Speaker, 1645
works.source: Oliver Cromwell · The Letters and Speeches of Oliver Cromwell, ed. Carlyle (Lomas edition) · public domain
works.note: His report to Parliament after the decisive victory at Naseby, ending with a bold plea for liberty of conscience for the men who had fought.

works.section: Cromwell, as told by David Hume
works.title: The Dissolution of the Rump Parliament, 1653
works.source: David Hume, The History of England (Part E: From Charles I to Cromwell) · Project Gutenberg #19215 · public domain
works.note: Hume’s account of the day Cromwell marched in and expelled the Long Parliament by force — preserving his own blunt words: “give place to honester men… take away this bauble.”

works.section: Cromwell, as told by David Hume
works.title: Cromwell Made Lord Protector, 1653
works.source: David Hume, The History of England (Part E: From Charles I to Cromwell) · Project Gutenberg #19215 · public domain
works.note: The Instrument of Government and Cromwell’s elevation to supreme power as Lord Protector of the Commonwealth.

works.section: Cromwell, as told by David Hume
works.title: The Death and Character of Cromwell, 1658
works.source: David Hume, The History of England (Part E: From Charles I to Cromwell) · Project Gutenberg #19215 · public domain
works.note: Hume’s celebrated character sketch — the great historian’s verdict on Cromwell’s genius, ambition, and the tangle of enthusiasm and policy in his nature.

works.title: Hume, History of England — Charles I to Cromwell
works.note: The full volume covering the Civil War and Commonwealth.
